claim: Bulk-tissue RNA (HPA 'RNA expression (HPA)' product, 40 tissues -- not the separate 51-tissue 'consensus' product) shows CEACAM5 predominantly enriched in GI tissues (colon 920.3, rectum 885.1, appendix 175.2, stomach 154.1, esophagus 148.8 nTPM), with additional non-GI RNA signal requiring follow-up: lung 28.5 nTPM (above small intestine's 23.2) and tonsil 34.6, smooth muscle 26.8 nTPM. See TE003 (HPA IHC) for the cell-type-resolved follow-up on lung specifically. Liver/heart/kidney/bone marrow all <1 nTPM.
notes: Bulk RNA only -- does not by itself confine the signal to GI tissue (see TE003 for the IHC evidence, which does not corroborate the lung/tonsil/smooth-muscle RNA signal at High/Medium protein level -- lowering, not eliminating, that concern). indication_id is this repository's territory for the matched primary/CRLM cohorts this normal-tissue reference is paired against (Module B, same target, currently BLOCKED); the source data itself (HPA) is not mCRC-patient-specific -- see adc_decision_axis=normal_tissue_risk, a cross-patient reference axis.

claim: GTEx v11 median TPM (68 tissues) is consistent with enrichment in mucosa-containing/epithelial-enriched samples: Colon_Transverse_Mucosa 1069.6 vs Colon_Transverse_Muscularis 75.4 (>10x), Esophagus_Mucosa 277.8 vs Esophagus_Muscularis 0.14 (>1000x). This is bulk RNA, evidence_directness=UNCALIBRATED_PROXY -- it cannot by itself support a specifically-epithelial-cell claim (see TE003's HPA IHC row for that). Colon_Sigmoid (0.74) vs Colon_Transverse (243.7) is an unexplained within-organ discrepancy in this source, recorded as open, not resolved by assumption. Liver/heart/kidney all <0.1 median TPM; GTEx v11 has no bone marrow tissue.
notes: REFERENCE_SUPPORT tier per module_classification.tsv -- catches normal-organ signal HPA might miss, cannot alone establish a safety conclusion. nTPM (HPA, TE001) and median_TPM (GTEx, this row) are not directly comparable across rows; each source's pattern is read within itself, not cross-normalized.

claim: HPA cell-type-resolved normal-tissue IHC (109 tissue/cell-type rows for CEACAM5) is High only in Appendix/Colon/Rectum enterocytes (incl. microvilli), endocrine cells and goblet cells (12 rows), and Medium only in mucosal lymphoid cells (Colon/Rectum), squamous epithelial cells (Esophagus/Oral mucosa), and glandular cells (Stomach) (6 rows). Every other scored cell type, including lung alveolar cells type I and type II (both Low), bone marrow hematopoietic cells (Low), tonsil and smooth muscle (not scored High/Medium anywhere), is Low or Not detected. This does not corroborate TE001's flagged lung/tonsil/smooth-muscle RNA signal at High/Medium protein level in the scored cell types, which lowers -- but does not eliminate -- the normal-tissue concern: HPA's cell-type panel is not exhaustive, and a Low IHC score is not zero accessible surface antigen.
structured_value: High(12 rows)=Appendix/Colon/Rectum:{enterocytes,enterocytes-Microvilli,endocrine cells,goblet cells};Medium(6 rows)=Colon/Rectum:mucosal lymphoid cells,Esophagus/Oral mucosa:squamous epithelial cells,Stomach:glandular cells;Low_or_NotDetected=91 rows incl. Lung alveolar I/II=Low, Bone marrow hematopoietic cells=Low
notes: This is Module E's core protein/IHC-first triage evidence (not the RNA-only screen TE001/TE002 are), per module README. evidence_directness=UNCALIBRATED_PROXY, not CALIBRATED_PROXY -- there is no target-specific quantitative surface assay, flow-cytometry antigen-density calibration, or IHC-to-surface-density mapping backing this row; IHC is closer to real biology than bulk RNA but is not itself a calibration step. IHC intensity is not a quantitative surface-density assay and cannot by itself establish accessible antigen density or a therapeutic window (see module README Cannot-prove section). Mucosal lymphoid cells at Medium are immune infiltrate, not epithelium -- read as a distinct finding, not folded into the epithelial pattern.

claim: Within GSE178318's 6 matched primary-CRC/liver-metastasis patient pairs, marker-score-typed epithelial cells (validated against 3 PBMC samples typing 89.5-94.4% immune, ~0% epithelial) show detectable CEACAM5 in every patient's epithelial compartment in both primary and metastatic tissue: 11 of 12 samples bucket RNA_low (12.8%-47.7% of epithelial cells CEACAM5-positive), 1 (COL12_LM) buckets RNA_high (66.7%), none bucket RNA_no. Between-patient heterogeneity is substantial (12.8%-66.7% range); primary-to-LM direction is a 3-vs-3 split across the 6 patients, not a consistent trend either way.
notes: This is marker-gene-score cell-compartment typing (cell_type_marker_set_v1.tsv), NOT malignancy calling -- no CNV inference or matched-normal comparison distinguishes malignant from normal/reactive epithelium within these tumor-site specimens; 'epithelial cell in a PRIMARY_CRC/LIVER_METASTASIS specimen' is used as the closest available proxy for malignant epithelium, not a confirmed call. n=6 patients is within-cohort descriptive, not population prevalence (Module B's own Cannot-prove). Cohort composition caveat: indication_id=mcrc_preop_chemotherapy_crlm matches Module E's tgt_ceacam5 dossier for this same target, but only 3 of these 6 patients (COL15/COL17/COL18) actually received preoperative chemotherapy per sample_map.tsv -- the other 3 (COL07/COL12/COL16) are treatment-naive; all 6 are matched primary/CRLM pairs (this indication node's anatomy/timing scope) but the treatment-exposure criterion in its name does not describe half the cohort. GSE225857 (this module's other CORE_ACTIVE dataset) remains blocked on CNSA access -- this row covers GSE178318 only.
